records.sourceAnchor: Udyam MSME, identified energy-intensive cluster/sector, eligible energy-efficiency project, loan and lender route, interest subvention, audit/DPR support and 10% savings condition
observations: BEE describes ADEETIE as a Ministry of Power initiative providing technical handholding and conditional financial support for energy-efficient technology adoption by MSMEs.

The current BEE page identifies Udyam-registered MSMEs in 60 identified energy-intensive clusters across 14 sectors, with a requirement to demonstrate at least 10% energy savings from implemented technologies.

The scheme describes 5% interest subvention for Micro/Small enterprises and 3% for Medium enterprises; this is applied to eligible lender finance and is not itself a grant or guaranteed loan approval.
Investment-grade energy audit/DPR reimbursement, technical handholding and monitoring/verification are separate support tracks and must not be added to interest subvention as one total benefit.

The programme period is FY 2025-26 through FY 2027-28. EOI, cluster availability, technology eligibility, registered financial institutions, minimum-net-interest wording and annual claim rules require current guideline reconciliation before an actionable recommendation.
reviewFollowUps: Verify active Udyam status, identified cluster, covered sector, current technology list and any phased expansion before matching.
Confirm eligible loan range, debt-funding percentage, lender approval, subvention calculation, minimum-net-interest condition and claim timing.
Verify audit/DPR reimbursement caps, empanelled auditors, DPR format, commissioning evidence and 10% savings measurement/verification.
Check current EOI route, registered financial institutions, operation guideline, scheme amendments, portal status and grievance route.
Keep loan principal, interest subvention, audit/DPR reimbursement and energy-cost savings separate; obtain a human reviewer decision before publication.

records.sourceAnchor: Pages 1-4: mission objectives, five-year period, funding, startup pilots, selection and IP modalities
observations: The Ministry of Power and Ministry of New and Renewable Energy established MAHIR for indigenous development and demonstration of advanced energy-sector technologies.
The Office Memorandum provides for outcome-linked funding, calls/RFPs, Technical Scoping Committee screening, Apex Committee approval and pilot projects of technologies developed by Indian startups.

The CPRI programme page identifies the research domains, records the first call as closed and says a second call will be advertised soon. The first-call PDF sets 20 January 2024 as the submission deadline.

The first call invited academia, industry, utilities, startups and R&D institutions and required substantial research and innovation, technical and financial particulars, milestones, deliverables and institutional declarations.
The Office Memorandum states that IP in developed technology is shared with the Government of India and research agency, and startup pilots have applicable IP-sharing conditions.
